violation.message: Undo is sheet-unaware: after adding a sheet mid-window (auto-switching to it) and performing further actions, undo-all neither removes the added sheet nor restores the active sheet, and cell-level undo transactions appear to apply to whichever sheet is currently active rather than the sheet they were recorded on. 14 digest differences after undo-all: activeSheet 0->1, sheetNames[1] persists, multiple sheets[0] cells diverge.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: Undo transactions do not record a sheet index; apply_changes in undo_commands.rs operates on state.grid (the active-sheet mirror). Sheet add/delete/rename push no undo entries and do not clear the stack, so undo walks 'through' a sheet boundary applying changes to the wrong sheet. Either make sheet ops undoable with sheet-aware transactions, or (Excel parity) have sheet structural ops clear the undo stack.

filesChanged: app/src-tauri/src/sheets.rs (invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure + the five structural commands; remap_sheet_keyed_stores no longer re-aims queued undo entries; move_sheet/copy_sheet release their guards first)

fix.diffSummary: ROOT: the third appearance of one missing dimension. `CellChange::SetCell` had already grown a `sheet` field, but the field holds an INDEX -- a POSITION, not an identity. Deleting, moving or copying a sheet renumbers every index after it, so a queued undo entry silently came to describe a different sheet and undo wrote onto a sheet the user never edited. `remap_sheet_keyed_stores` re-aimed the `CustomRestore` payloads and NOT the `SetCell` indices beside them in the same transactions, so it repaired half the problem. Two hazards were not about indices at all: a RENAME shifts nothing but rewrites every formula in the workbook, leaving queued `previous` cells holding ASTs that spell the old sheet name; and the width/height/merge/snapshot changes carry no sheet dimension AT ALL. VERIFIED EXCEL BEHAVIOUR: Excel does not let a sheet structural operation be undone -- deleting a worksheet is the documented case ('you can't undo deleting sheets') and no undo entry exists for inserting, renaming, moving or copying one either -- so a workbook-structure change ends the undo history. Under the standing 'Excel parity wins' rule that is now Calcula's behaviour, applied at ONE choke point that all five commands call, with a source census that fails by name when a command stops calling it. It also answers the target-sheet-deleted case with Excel's own answer instead of an invented one: the question cannot arise, because the delete ended the history that could have asked it. The MCP tool layer had been TELLING callers this all along ('Sheet structure changes are NOT undoable') while leaving the stack intact behind them. Removing the re-aim also removed a real lock-order inversion: it took `undo_stack` while `move_sheet`/`copy_sheet` held the grid pair, the reverse of `apply_changes`. Finally, the soak oracle could not tell 'a sheet operation ended the history' from 'the walk undid past its checkpoint' -- which is exactly how this bug was FILED -- so `UndoStack` now counts wholesale clears separately from cap evictions and `stepsBackToBaseline` names the right cause.

Calcula kept TWO records of one thing: `Table.style_options.show_filter_button` (persisted, on the table) and the entry in `auto_filters` (persisted separately in autofilters.json). `create_table` wrote both; `remove_auto_filter` cleared only the second. `Table.auto_filter_id` is derived state that is never saved, so the load path reconstructs it -- and finding no saved filter for a sheet whose table STILL advertised buttons, it seeded one from that table. The removal was undone by the reopen. EXCEL PARITY SETTLES THE DESIGN: Excel has a single state, `ListObject.ShowAutoFilter`. Data > Filter (Ctrl+Shift+L) on a table and Table Design > Filter Button are the same switch, and turning it off persists. There is no Excel state where a table shows filter dropdowns but has no filter. So `remove_auto_filter_inner` now clears `show_filter_button` on the table that OWNED the removed filter (matched by exact id, so bystander tables on the same sheet keep their own buttons). (b) `sheet_index_to_id` now returns `Option<SheetId>` and (c) `sheet_id_to_index` returns `Option<usize>`; all 29 call sites drop the orphan instead. violation.message: UNDO OF AN OFF-SHEET EDIT IS INVISIBLE. Excel keeps ONE undo history and switches to the sheet the undone action happened on, so the user sees what changed. Calcula restored the right cells on the right sheet (BUG-0034 fixed that) and then said nothing at all: the tab strip, the grid, the formula bar and every piece of per-sheet chrome stayed on the sheet the user happened to be looking at. An undo of an edit made on another sheet was therefore indistinguishable from an undo that did nothing -- the value moved, correctly, on a sheet nobody could see. Named as still-open in the register at 9f and deferred there because a backend-only switch would show Sheet1's tab over Sheet2's data, which is worse than the silence.

repro.description: THREE ORDINARY ACTIONS. (1) Click the Sheet2 tab and type a value into Sheet2!A1. (2) Click the Sheet1 tab. (3) Press Ctrl+Z. Before: nothing on screen changes -- the value on Sheet2 is correctly restored, but the app stays on Sheet1 and reports no switch, so there is no way to tell the undo happened. After: the app switches to Sheet2, selects A1, and the tab strip, grid, formula bar, column widths, row heights, hidden rows, merges, zoom, split and freeze panes all land on Sheet2 together. Redo behaves the same way. Unit-level reproduction: undo_commands::undo_sheet_activation_tests::an_undo_of_an_off_sheet_edit_activates_that_sheet.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: `UndoResult` had no sheet dimension at all, so the frontend could not have followed a switch even if the backend had made one, and `sheets::set_active_sheet` was a Tauri command taking `State<AppState>` -- unreachable from `apply_changes`, which holds an `&AppState`. Both halves were needed: the backend performing a REAL activation through the one implementation that swaps every per-sheet store, and the frontend following it through the same channel a tab click uses.

fix.diffSummary: `Transaction::target_sheet()` answers WHICH sheet a transaction belongs to (first recorded change that carries one; None for a CustomRestore-only transaction, whose sheet is inside opaque bytes). `sheets::set_active_sheet` is now a one-line delegation to `sheets::activate_sheet(&AppState, index)`, the single implementation of the swap -- grid mirror, column widths, row heights, merged regions, user-hidden rows/cols, then the dependency-map rebuild. `apply_changes` calls it AFTER the restore and with no lock held, so the whole off-sheet path (deferred geometry, grids[sheet] writes, recalc_after_off_sheet_write) still runs and is still exercised by the BUG-0034 guards; the mirror swap then picks up exactly the stores those arms wrote. A HIDDEN target is restored but NOT activated -- Excel cannot make a hidden sheet active, and following it would put the grid on a sheet with no tab. `UndoResult` gains activeSheetIndex / activeSheetName / restoredAnchor, reported unconditionally so the frontend compares against its own state. The frontend follows through the tab click's OWN channel (sheet:beforeSwitch, the grid sheet context, sheet:normalSwitch, SHEET_CHANGED) with no await between the dispatches, and aims the selection at the restored anchor. handleUndo and handleRedo -- previously byte-identical copies -- are now one `applyRestoreToTheView`.

Each holds what the other waits for. violation.message: HIDING THE ACTIVE SHEET LEAVES THE BACKEND ON THE HIDDEN SHEET, SO EDITS GO TO THE WRONG SHEET. `hide_sheet` set the visibility flag and RETURNED a recommended new active index without touching `state.active_sheet` or any per-sheet mirror -- its own doc comment said "frontend should call set_active_sheet if it changed". None of the three callers did: `SheetTabs.handleHide` passes `backendHandledSwitch: true` ("Backend already swapped - just sync frontend state"), `ScriptNotebook/lib/deferredActionHost.setSheetVisibility` comments "Hiding the active sheet makes the backend switch", and the broker's `api.setSheetVisibility` goes through `announceSheetsChanged`, which dispatches `setActiveSheet` into the frontend store. All three therefore moved the FRONTEND onto the recommended sheet while the backend still had the hidden sheet active -- and every cell read and every cell write goes to the active sheet. The tab strip highlights Sheet1, the canvas paints Sheet2's data, and typing writes into the sheet the user just hid. Excel's rule settles it: a hidden sheet cannot be the active sheet (no tab to select; `Activate` raises in VBA).

repro.description: TWO ACTIONS. (1) Add a sheet (which makes it active). (2) Right-click its tab and choose Hide. Before: the tab strip and the grid claim to be on Sheet1 while `get_active_sheet` still answers with the hidden sheet, so `get_cell_value`/`update_cell` operate on it -- typing appears to edit Sheet1 and edits the hidden sheet. After: the backend performs the switch through `activate_sheet`, so the index, the grid mirror, the column widths, the row heights, the merged regions and the user-hidden sets all move together. Unit-level: `sheets::hidden_active_sheet_tests::{hiding_the_active_sheet_activates_a_visible_one, the_grid_mirror_moves_with_it, the_sheet_it_lands_on_is_visible}`. NOTE: `TestRunner`'s "Hide and unhide a sheet" hides the sheet it has just added -- i.e. the ACTIVE sheet -- every time it runs, and asserted only `visibility == "hidden"`, so the defect sat underneath a passing test.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: A command that returns a RECOMMENDATION into a codebase where every caller reads it as a report of what happened. The four other sheet-structure commands (`add`, `delete`, `move`, `copy`) all write `active_sheet` and swap the mirrors themselves; `hide_sheet` was the only one that did not, and the asymmetry was invisible because the return type is identical.

fix.diffSummary: `hide_sheet` splits into a `hide_sheet_inner(&AppState, &FileState, ..)` body (so the switch has a unit tier) that computes the target with every guard scoped to a block, releases them, and then calls `activate_sheet` -- the ONE implementation of the swap, the same one BUG-0043 extracted. A source census fails the build if it ever assigns `active_sheet` itself instead. SECOND DEFECT, found by the test fixture: `ensure_vec_len(&mut sheet_visibility, n)` pads with `String::default()`, i.e. the EMPTY STRING, while every reader compares against the literal "visible" -- `SheetTabs` renders `sheets.filter(s => s.visibility === "visible")`, `hide_sheet` counts the visible sheets that way, and `next_sheet`/`previous_sheet` skip anything else. A padded slot is therefore a sheet with no tab that the workbook believes is neither hidden nor visible, and `build_sheet_list`'s `.unwrap_or("visible")` cannot repair it because the slot is `Some("")` rather than `None`. All four padding sites go through a new `ensure_visibility_len`. INSTRUMENT: the walker snapshot now carries `backendActiveSheet` and `sheetVisibility`, and a new cheap invariant `active-sheet-agrees` fails the walk when the two halves of the app name different active sheets, or when the active sheet is not visible -- a class no digest oracle can see, because the digest is assembled entirely from AppState and a backend that is wrong in a self-consistent way passes all three. `sheet.hide` is now a walker action.

violation.message: TABLES DO NOT FOLLOW THEIR SHEET THROUGH A MOVE OR A COPY. `state.tables` is keyed by sheet INDEX, and it is the one sheet-index-keyed store that is NOT in `remap_sheet_keyed_stores` -- `delete_sheet` re-keys it inline, because the same pass has to drop the deleted sheet's table NAMES out of `table_names` and a generic remap cannot do that half. `move_sheet` and `copy_sheet` therefore re-keyed every OTHER per-sheet store (comments, scenarios, outlines, conditional formats, data validations, cell types, controls, protection, AUTOFILTERS, spill tracking, reports, and the floating slicer/timeline/chart/sparkline stores) and left this one where it was. The measured symptom is the AutoFilter link, because `auto_filters` DID move: on reload `relink_autofilter_owner` looks for the owning table under the filter's sheet index, finds none, and the link is gone (`tables.<id>.autoFilterId: <id> -> <absent>`) -- or worse, finds a DIFFERENT sheet's table and hands it the filter (`<A> -> <B>`, seed 90070001; `<absent> -> <id>`, seed 90070002). The lost link is only the visible half. The table itself is now registered against another sheet, and that registry is what every structured reference (`=SUM(Table1[Amount])`) resolves through, what the save path writes per sheet, and what the AutoFilter, totals-row and calculated-column commands look the table up in.

violation.message: DELETING A SHEET CAN LEAVE A WORKBOOK WITH NO VISIBLE SHEET, AND CAN LEAVE THE ACTIVE SHEET ON A HIDDEN ONE. `hide_sheet` has always refused to hide the last VISIBLE sheet; `delete_sheet` only ever checked that at least one SHEET remained (`sheet_names.len() <= 1`). Hide Sheet1, delete Sheet2, and that guard is satisfied while the workbook is left with a single HIDDEN sheet: no tab to click, and an active index naming a sheet the user cannot look at. Excel's wording is exactly the distinction it was missing -- "a workbook must contain at least one visible worksheet". Separately, the index arithmetic that picks the post-delete active sheet is pure bookkeeping, so deleting the sheet beside a hidden one lands the user ON the hidden one even when other visible sheets exist.

repro.description: TWO ACTIONS, from the sheet tab context menu. (1) Right-click Sheet1 > Hide. (2) Right-click Sheet2 > Delete. Before: the delete succeeds and the workbook has one sheet, hidden -- the tab strip is empty and the grid is showing a sheet with no tab. After: the delete is refused with "Cannot delete the last visible sheet". The second half: with three sheets, hide Sheet2, then delete Sheet3 -- before, the active index lands on the hidden Sheet2; after, it walks on to a visible one. Unit-level: `sheets::hidden_active_sheet_tests::{a_delete_that_would_leave_no_visible_sheet_is_counted_as_zero, the_landing_sheet_skips_a_hidden_preference, delete_sheet_asks_both_questions}`.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: "At least one sheet" and "at least one VISIBLE sheet" are different tests, and only one of the two commands that can violate the rule was making the right one. The asymmetry survived because `delete_sheet` takes eight `State<T>` arguments and cannot be driven from a unit test, so the rule was never asked of it.

fix.diffSummary: Two pure functions with their own unit tier -- `visible_sheets_after_removing` (the refusal) and `nearest_visible_sheet` (the landing) -- plus `sheet_is_visible`, which reads a SHORT `sheet_visibility` as visible exactly as `build_sheet_list` does. `delete_sheet` calls both, and a source census (`delete_sheet_asks_both_questions`) fails the build if either call goes away, because the command itself cannot be tested directly. Non-vacuity partners pin that the landing walk is a no-op when the preferred sheet is already visible, and that a short visibility vector does not make a workbook undeletable.

source.runId: soak walk seed 1786446166374 (200 actions), on the build that had just fixed BUG-0047

violation.message: THE UNDO ORACLE REPORTS A FALSE PRODUCT DEFECT WHEN A SHEET IS ADDED WHILE THE UNDO HISTORY IS EMPTY. Measured: "Undoing 22 steps did not restore the checkpoint state. 2 differences; first: sheetNames[2]: \"<absent>\" -> \"Sheet3\"" -- and both digest differences were that one EMPTY sheet. The walk had ADDED Sheet3 inside the checkpoint window; adding a sheet is not undoable (Excel parity, BUG-0005), so no number of undo steps returns to the checkpoint and the window is not decidable. The oracle decided it anyway. `stepsBackToBaseline` asks whether a wholesale clear DISCARDED anything (`clearedTotal`, a count of TRANSACTIONS), and a structure change made while the stack is already empty discards nothing -- so the counter does not move, the oracle sees no clear, winds the history back and reports the sheet the walk added as an undo defect. This is the exact false alarm BUG-0005's fix removed for the non-empty case, on the one case it left standing; it is a harness defect, and its cost is a triage cycle plus a lost walk each time it fires.

repro.description: Any walk that (a) reaches a checkpoint with an empty or freshly-cleared undo stack, (b) pushes some ordinary transactions, and (c) adds/deletes/renames/moves/copies a sheet in the same window. Seed 1786446166374 at 200 actions does it at the checkpoint after step 125. Deterministic unit-level reproduction: `undoHistoryHorizon.test.ts::says so when the clear discarded NOTHING because the stack was empty` -- baseline {clearedTotal: 4, clearsTotal: 1}, now {clearedTotal: 4, clearsTotal: 2}: `clearedTotal` has not moved and the window must still be undecidable. Its partner covers the non-empty-baseline branch. Sabotage-checked: reverting the decision to `cleared > 0` fails exactly those two.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The counter answered a question next to the one that was being asked. `cleared_total` was introduced to tell "a structure change ended the history" from "the cap dropped it" and "the walk undid past it", and it does -- as long as the history had something in it. The fact the caller actually needs is whether a clear HAPPENED, which is not the same number.

fix.diffSummary: `UndoStack` gains `clears_total`, incremented on EVERY `clear()` regardless of what it discarded, alongside the transaction-counting `cleared_total` -- kept separate so `no_phantom_clear_on_a_pristine_workbook` keeps meaning what it says. `get_undo_state` reports it as `clearsTotal`; `stepsBackToBaseline` decides on `clears > 0` and uses `cleared` only to say how much was lost ("1 clear(s), 0 transaction(s) discarded"). Two new cases in `undoHistoryHorizon.test.ts` cover both branches (empty and non-empty baseline) with `clearedTotal` deliberately unchanged, and they fail when the decision is reverted.

violation.message: SHEET VISIBILITY (AND TAB COLOUR) ARE PERSISTED MUTATIONS WITH NO UNDO ENTRY AND NO HISTORY INVALIDATION. Measured: "Undoing 26 steps did not restore the checkpoint state. 1 differences; first: sheets[1].visibility: \"visible\" -> \"hidden\"" -- the sheet was VISIBLE at the checkpoint, the walk hid it inside the window, and undoing the whole window left it hidden. `hide_sheet`, `unhide_sheet` and `set_tab_color` all construct `DocumentEffect::mutates` (the state IS saved into the .cala), take no `undo_stack`, record nothing, and -- unlike the five structural commands -- do not call `invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure` either. THE DEFECT IS REAL UNDER EITHER PARITY READING, and only the fix differs: if Excel undoes a sheet hide (which is the author's reading, at moderate confidence -- the Undo button is available after Format > Hide & Unhide > Hide Sheet), the commands owe an undo entry that restores `sheet_visibility` / `tab_colors`; if it does not, they owe the history invalidation the other sheet commands make, so the oracle declines the window instead of deciding it. What is NOT defensible is the current third state, where the history stays intact across a change undo cannot reverse.

repro.description: THREE ACTIONS. (1) Type a value into Sheet1!A1. (2) Right-click Sheet2's tab and choose Hide. (3) Press Ctrl+Z. The cell edit is undone and Sheet2 stays hidden, with no indication that anything was skipped -- and pressing Ctrl+Z again walks further back through a history that no longer describes the workbook. Same shape for Unhide and for a tab colour. Walk-level: E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_SEED=90070001 SOAK_ACTIONS=250 SOAK_CATEGORY_WEIGHTS="sheet:10" SOAK_ORACLE_EVERY=25 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep "random walk" -- fails at the checkpoint after step 125. NOT SUPPRESSED: no `KNOWN_ISSUES` entry was added, so sheet-weighted walks will keep reporting it until it is decided.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: CONFIRMED, and the OWNER CALL is decided in favour of an undo ENTRY. The two candidates were 'record a CustomRestore' and 'end the history the way the five structural sheet commands do', and what settles it is that the argument FOR ending the history does not reach these three. Read `invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure`'s own doc: the five end the history because an undo entry names its sheet by INDEX and those five RENUMBER every index (or, for a rename, rewrite every formula that spells the name), so a queued entry silently comes to describe a different sheet. Hiding a sheet renumbers nothing and rewrites nothing -- it assigns one element of a parallel Vec in place -- so every queued entry still describes exactly the sheet it was recorded on, and the hazard the invalidation exists to prevent is ABSENT. With the structural argument gone what remains is an asymmetry of cost: ending the history destroys every undo step the user had accumulated, recording an entry costs a few bytes. `hide_sheet_inner` already takes that same cheap direction one line over for the dirty flag ('a false positive, which is the cheap direction').
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src-tauri/src/sheets.rs (hide_sheet_inner, unhide_sheet, set_tab_color) — either a `CustomRestore` payload for `sheet_visibility` / `tab_colors` plus its apply arm in undo_commands.rs, or a call to `invalidate_undo_history_for_sheet_structure`. OWNER CALL: which one is Excel parity.

fix.diffSummary: A new `"sheet_tab_state"` CustomRestore kind carries `{ visibility, tab_colors, active_sheet }` -- whole vectors (their LENGTH is state: `ensure_visibility_len` pads them lazily and `build_sheet_list` reads them by index, so a partial restore could leave the list disagreeing with itself), each field `Option` so 'this change did not touch it' is expressible, exactly like `UserHiddenSnapshot`. `hide_sheet_inner`, `unhide_sheet_inner` and `set_tab_color_inner` record it; the latter two are NEW `_inner` splits, added for the same reason `hide_sheet_inner` exists (a `State<T>` command has no unit tier). Every recording happens with NO other state lock held -- `record_custom_restore` takes `undo_stack`, which the crate's canonical order puts ahead of the grid locks -- and only when something actually changed, so a no-op hide/unhide/recolour and a REFUSED hide burn no undo step. Registry row: domain `Sheets` (the translator fans it out to "sheets:refresh" + SHEET_CHANGED, which is what makes the tab strip re-read), `defer: true` -- not a preference: undoing the hide of the ACTIVE sheet puts the user back through `sheets::activate_sheet`, which takes grid/grids/widths/heights/merges, all of which `apply_changes` still holds during the inline phase. `active_sheet` is recorded ONLY by hide (the only one that moves the user) and the restore refuses to follow it onto a sheet that is out of range or hidden, under the same rules as `activation_target`. 15 unit tests in `sheet_tab_state_undo_tests.rs` (undo/redo of all three, the standing-point follow and its non-active control, the hidden-target refusal, three no-op cases, a refused hide) plus a source census that every command recording persisted tab state names the kind, with a synthetic-source self-test proving the detector fires in both directions and that the brace matcher stops at the right function. `restore_registry_tests` (which fired on the new kind and had to be taught it) pins the domain and the defer flag. PROVED LIVE from a cold app through the REAL tab context menu and REAL Ctrl+Z (`sheet-tab-state-undo.spec.ts`): the hidden tab's absence is asserted FIRST so the probe is shown able to report the broken answer, then the tab returns, the backend and the rendered strip agree on the active index, and the formula bar reads a mark that only exists on the restored sheet. Paired control: undoing the hide of a NON-active sheet restores it and moves nobody.

violation.message: THE "TABLE DESIGN" CONTEXTUAL TAB SURVIVES THE DELETE OF THE LAST TABLE WHEN A SHEET HAS BEEN RENAMED IN BETWEEN. Measured: 'Contextual tab "Table Design" is visible but at least one table must exist. Found: slicers=0, charts=0, tables=0, pivots=0, timelines=0, sparklines=0'. The backend has NO tables and the ribbon still offers a tab whose every button addresses an object that no longer exists — the same end state BUG-0026 and the `syncDesignTabToTables` fix (soak seed 20260810) were about, reached through a door those fixes do not cover. The shrinker kept the rename: removing it makes the trace pass, so it is load-bearing and not incidental.

repro.description: FOUR ACTIONS, confirmed by the shrinker (30 replays, 22 clean passes, verdict=confirmed): `table.create` -> `sheet.rename {tabIndex: 0}` -> `table.select-into` -> `table.delete`. Replay: E2E_MANUAL=1 SOAK_TRACE=tests/regression/repros/BUG-0051.trace.json SOAK_EXPECT_FAIL=1 npx playwright test --project=soak --grep "Trace replay". NOTE ON REACHABILITY: renaming sheet 0 only became generatable in this pass — the walker's `sheet.rename` picked `pickInt(rng, 1, n-1)` and could never rename the first sheet, which is the one everything else refers to.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: ESTABLISHED, and it is NEITHER of the two filed candidates -- no probe was needed, the source says it. `deleteTableAsync` DOES succeed and DOES refresh its own cache; what it never does is announce the `objects` domain. The only thing that re-derives the contextual tab is `syncDesignTabToTables`, which runs on TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED, which is dispatched by the `objects` domain and by nothing else in the delete path. `announceObjectCascade` in the Table store named only ["slicer", "ribbonFilter"]; TWO CALLERS papered over it by emitting TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED BY HAND after awaiting the store (TableDesignTab's Delete and Convert-to-Range buttons), so the defect was invisible from the screen a human uses and reproducible from every other route -- a script, an MCP tool, the E2E walker. WHY THE CENSUS THAT EXISTS FOR THIS DID NOT CATCH IT: the two halves of `cascadeAnnouncementCensus.test.ts` contradicted each other. Its cascade half runs off `requiredDomainsFor`, which DELETES the owner's own domain from the required set on the reasoning that a route re-reading its own cache needs no announcement for itself -- and `objects` IS the Table's own domain. Its selection half, meanwhile, recorded in its own `why` that the tab 'is re-derived ... on TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED, which the `objects` domain dispatches'. One half excused exactly what the other half depended on. AND THE RENAME: the shrinker was right that removing `sheet.rename` made the trace pass, but it is not load-bearing to the DEFECT -- it was load-bearing to the SETUP. The walker's `table.create` used a raw `create_table` invoke, which leaves the frontend cache empty, so `table.select-into` could not register the tab at all; the rename fired SHEET_CHANGED, whose Table handler calls `refreshCache()`, and that -- nothing about renaming -- is what made the tab appear so it could then survive.
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/extensions/Table/lib/tableStore.ts (deleteTableAsync) + app/extensions/Table/index.ts (the SHEET_CHANGED handler, which refreshes the cache without re-deriving the tab) + app/extensions/Table/handlers/selectionHandler.ts

fix.diffSummary: The STORE announces its own domain change: `announceObjectCascade` becomes `announceTableObjectChange` and names ["objects", "slicer", "ribbonFilter"], so the delete and the convert-to-range make the identical announcement an out-of-band MCP table delete already made. The two hand-written TABLE_DEFINITIONS_UPDATED emits in TableDesignTab are DELETED -- they were a second source of truth for 'the table list changed' that only the button path had. THE CENSUS IS REPAIRED SO THE CLASS CANNOT RECUR: `SelectionOwner` gains `reconcileDomain` (the refresh domain whose fan-out reaches the reconciliation) and a mandatory `reconcileDomainWhy` for the null case, and a new rule `unannouncedReconciliations` requires EVERY delete route for that kind to announce it -- own domain or not, which is precisely the check `auditRoutes` structurally cannot make. Non-vacuity is asserted (exactly one owner exercises the rule today) and a synthetic-source teeth case proves the detector fires, that the fixed shape is accepted, that `ownDomain` + a self-refresh does NOT excuse it, and that a null domain with no reason is reported. The new rule immediately found a SECOND, INDEPENDENT instance -- but it was a false report: `announceObjectCascade` in `scriptHost/host.ts` reaches "objects" through a SECOND hop (`announceObjectsChanged`) that the analyser's one-hop rule did not follow. `domainsAnnounced` now follows announcement helpers transitively, which keeps the closure at 'the announcement helpers this route reaches' rather than the whole module. HARNESS: `table.create` in the walker goes through `createTableAsync` and emits TABLE_CREATED, the way Insert > Table does. The raw invoke it replaces left the frontend not knowing a table existed, which made the walk blind to the whole contextual-tab surface unless an unrelated action happened to refresh the cache. PROVED LIVE from a cold app: the ribbon is asserted to be SHOWING 'Table Design' before the delete (so 'it is gone' cannot pass vacuously), the backend is asserted to hold zero tables after it, and the rendered ribbon no longer offers the tab. TEETH: with the fix sabotaged on the running build and the WebView reloaded, the same live test reports `["Home", "Page Layout", "Controls", "Table Design"]` with zero tables; the file was then restored byte-identically (sha256 8ac813074b0b42914c0044001e22801efa3fa1940d88d30402d40199c10dc2bf) and it passes again. The committed 4-action trace `repros/BUG-0051.trace.json` now replays clean.

source.runId: live per-animation-frame sampling in app/e2e/journeys/sheet-tab-state-undo.spec.ts, written to attack BUG-0043's atomicity claim rather than re-read it

violation.message: A SHEET SWITCH IS NOT ATOMIC ON SCREEN: for a two-frame window the tab strip paints the NEW sheet as active while the canvas is still painting the OLD sheet's cells. Measured per animation frame, with the strip's own painted font-weight and a canvas `getImageData` probe of a cell that has ink on one sheet and not the other: undo-of-an-off-sheet-edit 21-71 ms, an ORDINARY TAB CLICK 60-67 ms, across three runs on the same build. It is therefore NOT undo's defect -- `applyRestoreToTheView` deliberately reuses the tab click's channel and measures no worse than it, usually better -- but a property of every sheet switch in the app. `followBackendSheetActivation` dispatches sheet:beforeSwitch -> the grid sheet context -> sheet:normalSwitch with no `await` between them, so the tab strip repaints on the next frame; the canvas cannot repaint until `refreshCells()` has completed a backend round trip.

repro.description: TWO ACTIONS, no scripting. (1) On Sheet2, type something into D1 so the two sheets are visually distinguishable. (2) Click Sheet1's tab, then click Sheet2's tab while sampling. For ~60 ms the Sheet2 tab is bold and the grid below it still shows Sheet1. Automated: `E2E_MANUAL=1 npx playwright test --project=journey e2e/journeys/sheet-tab-state-undo.spec.ts --grep BUG-0043`, which PRINTS both windows ('[BUG-0043] torn window: tab click N ms, undo M ms') and asserts only that undo is no worse than the click plus 50 ms, and that both settle. Raising that to the absolute claim -- no torn frame at all -- fails today, which is how this was found.

triage.rootCauseHypothesis: The switch is atomic in STATE and sequential in PAINT. The tab strip derives from the grid sheet context and re-renders synchronously with it; the canvas has to fetch the new sheet's cells before it can draw them. Closing it means either fetching the target sheet's viewport BEFORE the context swap and committing both in one batch, or suppressing the canvas paint until the fetch lands (which trades a wrong sheet for a stale one -- no better). The first is a change to the ONE switch path every tab click, script, MCP tool and undo goes through, and the register's standing warning about that path is that the last time it had two hydration paths, the second was mount-only and painted sheet 1's panes on sheet 2.
triage.suggestedFixArea: app/src/core/components/Spreadsheet/useSpreadsheetSelection.ts (followBackendSheetActivation) and whatever consumes `sheet:normalSwitch` to refetch the viewport. NOT undo-specific: fixing it in applyRestoreToTheView alone would make undo differ from the tab click, which is the split BUG-0043 closed.

fix.diffSummary: FIXED 2026-08-14, by the register's own prescription -- fetch the target sheet's viewport BEFORE the context swap and commit both in one batch -- and the measurement found the tear had TWO mechanisms, not one. (1) THE CANVAS HALF: every switch initiator (SheetTabs' click/add/delete/applySheetsResult and applyRestoreToTheView for undo/redo) now awaits `primeSheetSwitch()` AFTER the backend switch and BEFORE the first dispatch; the prime runs GridCanvas's own registered prefetcher (same calculateFetchRange, same getViewportCells+getSpillRanges) into a one-shot handoff slot (`app/src/core/lib/sheetSwitchPrefetch.ts`, exposed to Shell via @api), and the EXISTING `sheet:normalSwitch` handler -- no second channel, no second hydration path -- takes the payload and commits it synchronously inside the dispatch turn; a `useLayoutEffect` then paints the canvas before the browser paints, so React commits strip and cells in ONE flush. The dispatch sequence itself still contains no `await` (the §13 atomicity discipline; the prime sits strictly before the first dispatch), a same-sheet undo primes nothing, and a missing/failed prime degrades to the old fetch-after-swap path, never to a wrong paint. A sheet-epoch guard in fetchCells discards any viewport response that straddled a switch (the backend answers for whichever sheet is active when it SERVES the call) and re-fetches via the existing deferral machinery. (2) THE STRIP HALF, which the prime alone exposed at 33 ms on undo: the strip's bold weight rendered from SheetTabs' LOCAL activeIndex, which a backend-initiated switch only reaches through the 'Syncing activeIndex with Redux' useEffect -- one flush AFTER the canvas painted. `paintedActiveIndex` now renders the highlight from the grid sheet context, making followBackendSheetActivation's standing comment ('the tab strip has no state of its own... it syncs its highlight from this') true of the pixels; local activeIndex remains for behaviour only. MEASURED with the committed probe, cold app, consistent bundle: before 60-67 ms (click) / 21-71 ms (undo); after 0 ms / 0 ms across five consecutive runs, and the spec now asserts the ABSOLUTE claim (tornWindowMs === 0 for both gestures) it could not before. Switch latency unmoved: landed-at 90-156 ms (click) / 52-83 ms (undo) vs the pre-fix canvas catch-up at ~98 ms. TEETH: with the prime sabotaged to a no-op on the running build, the raised test fails with 'tab click 64 ms' and samples showing the strip at t=112 ms over ink at t=191 ms -- the filed symptom exactly; restored byte-identically (sha256 a6b85099f95e07ebd43a6b1c0d8eba42484ad8f4139e3a961e955b60906873b7) and green again. 10 unit tests pin the handoff slot (exactly-once take, foreign-sheet refusal, staleness, disposal ownership, renderSignal bracketing). The atomicity unit suite (undoSheetActivation) passes unchanged -- the event sequence and detail shapes are untouched. CAUTION FOR FUTURE MEASUREMENT: under `tauri dev`, HMR cycles that reload sheetSwitchPrefetch.ts can split its module state across stale importer instances (prime writes into one, take reads another), which resurrects a ~30 ms tear that does NOT exist on a cold bundle -- measure this bug only on a verified cold launch.

violation.message: A BACKEND-INITIATED FLOATING-RANGE DELETE LEAVES A REPAINT WINDOW THAT RENDERS -- AND FETCHES -- THE DELETED ROW, LOGGING console.error FOR A BENIGN RACE. The @api wrapper's deleteFloatingRange (and a script's api.deleteFloatingRange through the broker -- both routes confirmed in source) deletes the backend row, announces MUTATION_REFRESH['floatingRanges'], and emits CELLS_UPDATED. violation.message: MCP START CLAIMS SUCCESS BEFORE THE SERVER CAN ACCEPT, AND A BIND FAILURE IS INVISIBLE. mcp_start (app/src-tauri/src/mcp/mod.rs) set running=true, returned 'MCP server started on port N', and only THEN -- on a freshly spawned thread that first creates a whole Tokio runtime -- bound the TCP listener. A client following the documented start -> status -> connect sequence can beat the bind and get ECONNREFUSED from a server that mcp_status reports as running:true with a valid bearer token. Under a loaded machine (test 265 of a 554-test ordered run) the E2E spec lost exactly that race; the run's own backend log shows the spec's cleanup mcp_stop ('Server stop requested', line 8267) landing BETWEEN 'Server starting' (8266) and 'Server listening' (8268), after the fetch had already been refused -- the newborn server then shut down having served nothing. Worse: an actual bind failure (port in use) was only a background log line -- the command had already returned success and `running` silently flapped back to false. A real user pasting the MCP config into Claude Desktop hits the same refused connection with no error surfaced anywhere.
